thread:
Carlos: follow-up from the ephemeral_headroom RFC. want to lock down sizing math and operator handoff semantics before we ship the canary.
Maya: quick TL;DR of the goal?
Carlos: avoid cold-starts on 2-60s spikes while preventing tenants from gaming warm capacity. ephemeral_headroom = short-lived padding that can be preempted first.
Jon: sizing question: do we compute headroom as time->tokens on control plane, or pass a time target and let operator convert to slots?
Carlos: leaning operator-convert. operator knows fragmentation/slot sizes. control plane supplies: "headroom_secs" and "max_headroom_pct".
Priya: packing wins are real. operator can pack slack into spare fractional capacity on nodes. central time->tokens loses that.
Maya: but if operator computes differently per-zone, fairness can diverge. control plane must keep global accounting and limits.
Carlos: agreed. plan: control plane keeps budget and QPS-derived hint. operator returns Allocation with fields: allocated_slots, headroom_slots, expiry_ts, preemptible=true. (we'll document shape).
Sam: eviction order: headroom slots must be first-to-preempt, short grace (3s) and no checkpointing. mark workload as "warm_padding" so metrics exclude it from steady-state SLOs.
Priya: good. also a safety cap: headroom_slots <= ceil(commit_slots * max_headroom_pct). prevents cost spikes.
Jon: metric pipeline: use EWMA(1m) for baseline and burst detector with 10s window for immediate headroom signals. sample config: ```
provisioning:
  headroom_secs: 25
  max_headroom_pct: 0.12
  burst_detector:
    window_secs: 10
    multiplier: 4
```
Maya: about decay: operator should attach expiry_ts per headroom allocation. Prefer absolute expiry rather than a sliding token decrement to avoid tricky reconcilation across restarts.
Carlos: yes, absolute expiry helps idempotency. when operator restarts it can reconcile by reading active allocations.
Sam: operator coordination: two models: (A) centralized control-plane intent broker, operator is dumb packer; (B) operator-owned decision with last-writer-wins intent snapshot. which do we pick?
Priya: (B) seems more robust for packing, but we need deterministic tie-breakers and priority weights to avoid nondeterministic preemption order across operators.
Jon: add a priority_weight in intent. operator must respect weight when picking preempt targets. Also snapshot intents into operator store so restarts keep the same view.
Maya: UX/billing: Console wants split view: steady usage vs headroom usage. add billing tag "headroom" on tokens. Product can then surface cost impact by tenant.
Carlos: orch-bot: rolling canary note: applied headroom=20s, max_headroom_pct=0.10 to autoscaler-canary at 2024-11-05T09:12Z.
Sam: quick simulation math: headroom_slots = ceil(EWMA_rate * target_latency_s * safety_factor). example: EWMA_rate=0.8 req/s, target_latency=1.5s, safety=1.2 => tokens=ceil(0.8*1.5*1.2)=ceil(1.44)=2 slots. floor to 1.
Priya: suggest we also include a min_floor_slots param per-tier to avoid rounding causing many tiny allocations.
Jon: observability: emit these events: IntentEmitted, AllocationReturned, HeadroomExpiry, HeadroomPreempted. include tenant, intent_id, allocation_id.
Maya: alerts: if headroom_hours > expected_budget for 6h, page on-cost or misconfigured detector.
Carlos: implementation tasks: 1) control plane RFC addon (headroom_secs, max_headroom_pct, priority_weight) - Ben to draft, 2) operator prototype (expiry-based allocations, preempt-first) - Jon to prototype, 3) Console billing tag + UX mock - Priya. I'll run canary and report telemetry.
Sam: test plan: synthetic bursts across 500 tenants, measure 95p cold-start latency and extra GPU-hours. aim for 50-80% reduction in cold-starts with <10% extra GPU-hours.
Priya: naming: "headroom" vs "padding" vs "ephemeral_headroom"? prefer ephemeral_headroom in API to be explicit. internal docs can say "headroom/padding".
Carlos: agree. final note: keep RPC field "headroom_compute_preference" (operator|controlplane) for experimentation. default=operator.
Maya: thanks. we'll reconvene after 1 week of canary. :thumbsup:
Carlos: thanks all.
